# OPCH Technical Analysis Report — 2026-10-07

## Executive Summary

OPCH (Option Care Health, Inc.) has undergone a violent, event-driven repricing. After a catastrophic single-day gap down on 2026-04-30 (close 26.87 → 20.33, roughly -24% on ~17.3M shares) and months of basing between ~$19.50 and ~$24.50, the stock gapped explosively on 2026-10-06 from a 23.37 close to 31.00 — a one-day move of roughly +32.7% on a massive 65.1M shares, then held essentially flat at 31.01 on 2026-10-07 on 19.4M shares. This is a classic news-driven repricing (consistent with an acquisition/takeover-style print: tight range, huge volume, flat follow-through day), not an organic trend acceleration. Technically the stock is now dramatically overbought and extended far above every meaningful moving average, but the price action shows acceptance, not rejection, at the new level.

## Trend Structure

- **Pre-shock regime (April):** OPCH traded ~$27–$29 before the 2026-04-30 collapse to ~$20. That event reset the entire chart.
- **Basing regime (May–September):** A ~$19.50–$24.50 range with a gradual upward drift. The 50 SMA rose steadily from ~21.76 (mid-August) to 23.92 now, confirming a healthy medium-term recovery trend. The 200 SMA, by contrast, kept declining (27.57 → 26.43) as it still digests the April crash — price spent the entire window below it.
- **Breakout (2026-10-06/07):** The two-day repricing put price at 31.01 — above the 200 SMA (26.43) for the first time in the dataset, ~29.6% above the 50 SMA (23.92), and ~20.7% above the 10 EMA (25.69). It also cleared the April pre-crash highs (~$29.80 on 2026-04-09), making ~$29.80–$30 the key former-resistance zone.

## Momentum

- **RSI = 83.70** — deep overbought. This is the highest reading in the lookback and reflects the gap, not a gradual climax. Overbought can persist after a fundamental repricing, but it argues against chasing at market.
- **MACD = 0.93, signal = 0.18, histogram = 0.75** — an enormous bullish crossover driven almost entirely by the last two sessions; MACD went from -0.21 (10-05) to +0.43 to +0.93. The histogram expansion is the largest in the window. Note the MACD signal line (0.18) is still far below the MACD line — the move is too new for trend indicators to have caught up.
- **10 EMA = 25.69** is still ~5.3 points below price — fast-moving averages will take days to normalize; mean-reversion traders will watch the gap between price and the 10 EMA.

## Volatility & Bands

- **Bollinger bands:** middle 24.19, upper 29.01, lower 19.38. Price at 31.01 is ~7% above the upper band — a full band-breakout. Even after the band widened from 24.70 (10-05) to 29.01, price closed above it again on 10-07.
- **ATR = 1.09**, up from ~0.64–0.70 through September — volatility has roughly doubled. Position sizing must account for ~$1+/day of expected range until it settles.

## Volume

- 65.1M shares on 10-06 and 19.4M on 10-07 versus a typical ~1.5–3M daily volume — a >20x volume event. The tight 10-07 range (30.99–31.06) on still-huge volume indicates two-sided acceptance near $31, which is characteristic of a deal-price or re-rated equilibrium rather than a speculative blowoff.

## Key Levels

- **~$31.00–31.11:** current acceptance zone / 10-06 high (31.11).
- **~$29.80–30.00:** April pre-crash swing high — first major support if the gap partially fills.
- **~$29.01:** Bollinger upper band — shallow first support.
- **~$26.43:** 200 SMA — deeper trend support.
- **~$23.37–23.92:** pre-gap closes / 50 SMA — a full gap-fill would be a bearish failure signal for the repricing.

## Actionable Insights

- **Momentum/long-bias traders:** The setup is a gap-and-hold. Chasing above 31.11 is buying >2σ extension; more conservative entries come on a pullback toward 29–30 that holds. RSI 83.7 says the risk/reward for fresh entries at market is poor.
- **Existing holders:** The flat follow-through on heavy volume is constructive. A common risk frame: trail stops beneath the 10-06 low (30.97) for tight risk, or beneath ~29.00 (upper band / April high zone) for swing risk, given ATR ~1.09.
- **Risk flags:** Event-driven gaps can retrace sharply if the catalyst (e.g., a deal) falls through. A close back below ~23.40 would negate the repricing. Also note the death-cross-era context: the 50 SMA (23.92) still sits well below the 200 SMA (26.43); only the raw price, not the average structure, is bullish.
- **Caveat:** No tool here shows the catalyst itself; the pattern (huge one-day gap, tight hold at a round level, enormous volume) strongly suggests a corporate event. Confirmation of the underlying news is essential before treating $31 as a durable floor.

## Key Points Table

| Dimension | Reading (2026-10-07, verified) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Close | 31.01 (was 23.37 on 10-05) | ~+32.7% two-session repricing |
| Volume | 65.1M (10-06), 19.4M (10-07) vs ~1.5–3M avg | Event-driven, accepted at new level |
| RSI | 83.70 | Deeply overbought; poor chase entry |
| MACD / Hist | 0.93 / 0.75 | Violent bullish crossover, very fresh |
| 10 EMA / 50 SMA / 200 SMA | 25.69 / 23.92 / 26.43 | Price far above all; first close above 200 SMA in dataset |
| Bollinger (mid/upper/lower) | 24.19 / 29.01 / 19.38 | Close above upper band = >2σ extension |
| ATR | 1.09 (~2x Sept norm) | Elevated vol; size positions accordingly |
| Support | 30.97 → 29.0–30.0 → 26.43 → 23.4 | Layered downside reference levels |
| Bias | Bullish but extended | Hold/trim-strength over fresh chasing |

Skipped: no news/fundamental catalyst check (no such tool available) — the ~$31 level's durability depends on the event driving the 10-06 gap.

# OPCH Sentiment Report — 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-07

## Source-by-source breakdown

### News (Yahoo Finance)
Unavailable for the period — the feed only serves recent items, so this is a data gap, not an absence of news. No institutional framing could be collected directly from this source.

### StockTwits — the only substantive source
26 most-recent messages: 3 Bullish (12%), 0 Bearish (0%), 23 unlabeled. The raw labeled ratio understates the actual tone: the unlabeled content is dominated by a single, unambiguous corporate event.

**The dominant event:** On Tuesday 2026-10-06, McKesson and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice signed a definitive agreement to take Option Care Health private at **$32.05/share in cash (~$5.8B enterprise value), a ~37% premium** to Monday's $23.37 close (cited via Reuters/WSJ by @KryptonResearch14). The stock ran ~33% to ~$31.00 on volume flagged at 12–40x normal (@STUnusualVolume, @CloudCapital).

Message themes, in order of frequency:
- **Deal coverage/spread discussion** (@KryptonResearch14 x2, @hi_tech_lowlife noting OPCH trades below deal price — 'here's the spread', @FactSheets, @TNNStockAnalysisNews): framing is event-driven and positive.
- **Top-gainers/momentum lists** (@topstockalerts x7+): OPCH repeatedly listed among day's biggest gainers — classic post-announcement momentum attention.
- **Technical snapshots** (@CloudCapital x2): price $31.00, RSI 83.7 flagged **overbought**, MACD bullish, tagged 'Mixed/Sideways' and 'High Volatility / High Risk' — a cautionary note inside otherwise positive flow.
- **Analyst/fundamental recap** (@sSwSs, Bullish-tagged): mixed analyst sentiment, ~1.9% YoY revenue growth, strong technicals.
- **Spam/low-signal** (@MingChoo 'Made $19K' pump, @Market_Pulse_Report videos): discount.
- **Peer-context** (@MikeyMcDermott): OPCH grouped with $RXO, $PTC as strategic takeouts 'at healthy EBITDA multiples' — frames the deal as part of an M&A wave, mildly validating the price paid.

Zero bearish tags. The only negative-leaning signals are mechanical (overbought RSI, below-deal-price trading implying deal-completion risk, not fundamental disagreement).

### Reddit (r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing)
Unavailable for the period — same recency limitation as Yahoo. No Reddit signal either way; this cannot be read as silence or disagreement.

## Cross-source divergences and alignments
Only one source returned data, so true divergence analysis isn't possible. Within StockTwits itself there is a mild internal tension: user-tagged sentiment and event coverage are uniformly positive, while automated technical posts flag overbought conditions and high risk. That is a divergence between *narrative* sentiment (bullish on the deal) and *positioning* risk (stock already near the $32.05 cap, limited upside remaining).

## Dominant narrative theme
**Cash buyout at $32.05.** Effectively every substantive message orbits the McKesson/CD&R take-private. Sentiment about OPCH is now really sentiment about merger-arb economics: how close the stock trades to $32.05, whether the deal closes, and the spread. Fundamental opinions about the business itself are nearly absent.

## Catalysts and risks
- **Catalyst:** deal completion / spread compression toward $32.05; any regulatory or shareholder-approval milestones.
- **Risk:** deal breaks or is delayed — downside back toward the ~$23 pre-deal level; RSI 83.7 overbought flag; stock already ~97% of the way to the cash cap, so remaining upside is structurally bounded (~3.4% gross).
- Sentiment here is asymmetric: bullish-but-capped. Treat the bullish reading as confidence in the deal, not in further upside beyond $32.05.

## Data-quality flags
Two of three sources (Yahoo news, Reddit) returned placeholders — coverage is thin and single-source. StockTwits sample is only 26 messages with just 3 labeled. Confidence is **medium**: the event itself is well-evidenced, but independent corroborating sentiment channels are missing.

# OPCH (Option Care Health, Inc.) — Fundamentals Report as of 2026-10-07

## Data availability note

Two requested feeds were withheld by the vendor for point-in-time integrity: the profile/market-data block (market cap, multiples, 52-week range — all served at today's values, which would leak post-2026-10-07 information) and insider transactions (no filing date available, so public-as-of status cannot be determined). The analysis below is built entirely on SEC EDGAR filings made on or before 2026-10-07, at the values filed then. The most recent quarter available is Q1 2026 (ended 2026-03-31).

## Company profile

Option Care Health, Inc. (OPCH) is the largest U.S. provider of home and alternate-site infusion services, delivering therapies (IV antibiotics, nutrition support, immunoglobulin, chronic inflammatory disease treatments) outside hospital settings. The business benefits structurally from the shift of care out of hospitals into lower-cost home settings, a large referral network, and payer relationships. Note: financials before 2019 largely reflect the legacy Walgreens Boots infusion business combined in 2019 — treat pre-2020 figures as historical context, not the current entity.

## Revenue and growth (income statement)

Revenue trajectory of the combined company (quarterly, $M):

- FY2019 quarters: ~$218M → ~$616M by Q4 (post-merger ramp)
- FY2021: $782M → $860M
- FY2022: ~$860M → $1,016M
- FY2023: $1,069M → $1,227M
- FY2024: $1,279M → $1,435M
- FY2025: $1,416M (Q1), $1,435M (Q2), then $1,351M in Q3 2025
- Q1 2026: $1,351M (vs $1,416M Q1 2025 — a ~4.6% year-over-year decline)

Actionable point: after years of consistent high-single-to-double-digit growth, revenue has stalled. Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 both printed ~$1,351M and both were year-over-year declines (Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025: −4.6%). This is the single most important fundamental change to flag for traders — the growth narrative has hit a wall, likely reflecting therapy mix shifts (e.g., lower reimbursement on certain drug categories) or volume pressure. No guidance data was available to attribute the cause.

## Profitability

- Gross profit: stable and growing — $262M in Q1 2026, ~19.4% gross margin, in line with the ~18–19% range of recent years. Gross economics are intact; the revenue shortfall is not a pricing collapse.
- Operating income: $73M in Q1 2026 vs $85M in Q1 2025 and $79–85M through FY2025. Operating margin compressed to ~5.4% (vs ~6.0% a year earlier).
- Net income: $45M in Q1 2026 vs $52M in Q1 2025 and $45–56M/quarter through FY2025 (excluding a one-off $114M in Q2 2024, likely a tax/item effect).
- Diluted EPS: $0.29 in Q1 2026 vs $0.31 in Q1 2025. FY2025 quarterly EPS ran $0.28–0.32, implying roughly $1.15–1.20 annualized.

Interpretation: the company remains solidly profitable, but the P&L now shows negative operating leverage — flat/declining revenue against a fixed cost base is squeezing margins. Traders should watch whether Q2/Q3 2026 filings show margin stabilization.

## Balance sheet (as of 2026-03-31, $M)

- Total assets: $3,380; Total liabilities: $2,029; Stockholders' equity: $1,351
- Cash and equivalents: $177 — down sharply from $413 at Q2 2025 and $233 at year-end 2025
- Current assets: $1,195 vs current liabilities: $730 — current ratio ~1.64, adequate liquidity
- Liability load: total liabilities have stayed in the $1.9–2.1B band since 2023; equity has plateaued around $1.33–1.43B since early 2024, implying buybacks/debt paydown offsetting retained earnings growth rather than balance-sheet expansion.

The cash drawdown in Q1 2026 (down ~$56M in the quarter, ~$236M from the Q2 2025 peak) is the main balance-sheet watch item — see cash flow below.

## Cash flow

Cash flow figures are cumulative YTD; Q1 columns are single quarters.

- Operating cash flow, Q1: 2023 +$90M, 2024 −$69M, 2025 −$7M, 2026 −$12M. OPCH has a recurring Q1 working-capital outflow season (the 2023 print was the exception). The −$12M Q1 2026 is unremarkable seasonally but adds to the cash decline.
- Full-year operating cash flow has been strong: $224M (2022), $320M (2023), $287M (2024), $223M (2025 through Q3 YTD).
- Capex is modest and predictable (~$25–35M/year), so operating cash flow converts well to free cash flow.
- Financing: large persistent outflows in 2024–2025 (−$123M and −$187M FY, −$161M through Q3 2025, −$34M in Q1 2026) — consistent with debt repayment and/or share repurchases. This is the main use of cash alongside operations.

## Key takeaways for traders

1. Growth inflection: revenue declined YoY in the two most recent reported quarters — a first for the combined company. Any thesis built on historical ~10% growth needs recalibration.
2. Margins under mild pressure, not broken: gross margin steady at ~19%; operating/net margins down ~60–100bps YoY. Watch for cost actions in upcoming filings.
3. Cash generation intact but cash balance shrinking: Q1 seasonal OCF outflow plus ongoing financing outflows (buybacks/debt paydown) cut cash to $177M. Liquidity is fine (current ratio 1.64), but the buffer is thinner.
4. No leverage alarm: liabilities stable ~$2B against $3.4B assets; equity stable ~$1.35B.
5. Missing signals: valuation multiples and insider activity could not be confirmed as of 2026-10-07 with available data — any decision should be cross-checked against market data and Form 4 filings from another source.

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case — OPCH (Option Care Health, Inc.)

Let me open with the thing the bear will have the hardest time arguing against: this is no longer a "hope the growth story works" stock. On 2026-10-06, McKesson and Clayton, Dubilier & Rice signed a **definitive agreement to take OPCH private at $32.05/share in cash — a ~$5.8B enterprise value and a ~37% premium** to the pre-announcement close. The stock repriced violently — 23.37 → 31.00 on 65.1M shares (>20x normal volume) — and then did the most important thing a gap can do: it *held*. The 10-07 session printed a 30.99–31.06 range on 19.4M shares. That's acceptance, not a blowoff. The market is telling you this level is real.

## The bull thesis in one line

OPCH is now a merger-arb-style instrument with a hard cash ceiling at $32.05, a defined downside zone, and a strategic buyer + top-tier PE sponsor validating the asset at a premium — the remaining spread (~3.4% gross to deal price) is compensation for deal-completion risk, not for business risk.

## Why the deal itself is bullish evidence

1. **Two sophisticated buyers just priced this business.** McKesson is a strategic acquirer who knows the drug channel and infusion economics better than any public-market analyst. CD&R is one of the most disciplined healthcare sponsors alive. They did diligence on the same "stalled growth" numbers the bear will cite — and paid a 37% premium anyway. That's a stronger fundamental endorsement than any sell-side note.

2. **The "growth stall" the bear will raise was already priced — and then some.** Yes, revenue declined YoY in Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 (~$1,351M vs $1,416M). But the deal values OPCH at ~$5.8B EV against a business still producing ~$220–320M annual operating cash flow, ~$45–56M quarterly net income, ~19% gross margins, capex of only ~$25–35M/yr. Buyers paid up for cash generation and market position, not for momentum. The bear's best fundamental point is real — and it's already inside the deal price.

3. **Structural advantages didn't disappear.** OPCH is the *largest* U.S. home/alternate-site infusion provider. Care shifting out of hospitals into lower-cost settings is a secular tailwind. Scale in referral networks and payer relationships is exactly what makes it attractive to McKesson — channel synergies a standalone can't capture. The takeout itself is proof the consolidation thesis was right (sentiment flagged OPCH alongside RXO and PTC as strategic takeouts "at healthy EBITDA multiples").

4. **The technical damage the bears loved is repaired.** Price sits above the 200 SMA for the first time in the dataset, above the April pre-crash highs (~$29.80), with a fresh MACD bullish cross. The April -24% collapse that defined this chart for five months has been fully retraced in two sessions. Whatever broke the stock in April, the market just re-rated it permanently higher.

## Pre-empting the bear

- **"RSI 83.7, it's overbought, don't chase."** Agreed on entry mechanics — and irrelevant to the thesis. Overbought oscillators measure extension, not value. With a $32.05 cash cap, the question isn't "is it extended?" it's "does the deal close?" Chasing above $31.11 is sloppy; accumulating toward the $29–30 former-resistance zone on any pullback is the disciplined bull entry.
- **"Revenue is declining."** Addressed above — margin compression is mild (~60–100bps), gross economics are intact, and cash conversion is strong. The acquirers saw the same filings.
- **"Cash balance shrank to $177M."** Driven by deliberate financing outflows (buybacks/debt paydown), not operational bleeding. Liquidity is fine at a 1.64 current ratio — and post-announcement, the equity's fate is the merger agreement, not the balance sheet buffer.
- **"Upside is capped at ~3.4%."** True — and that's the honest part of the bull case. This isn't a 10-bagger pitch. It's a high-probability, bounded-return setup where the bear case requires a deal break. If the bear wants to argue a signed McKesson/CD&R definitive agreement fails, they need evidence — financing, regulatory, shareholder-approval — none of which exists in our data.

## Risk framing (because bulls who ignore risk lose debates)

Downside on a deal break is real — back toward ~$23.40, roughly -24%. That's why sizing and entry matter: the bull case is strongest sized as a spread trade (capture $31 → $32.05) rather than a heroic growth bet. A close back below ~$23.40 would invalidate everything. Watch approval milestones, not the RSI.

## Bottom line

The bull case isn't that OPCH is a screaming growth stock — it's that two sophisticated buyers just told you what it's worth, the market accepted that verdict on historic volume, and the remaining path to $32.05 cash is a matter of deal mechanics, not business performance. Sentiment is uniformly positive (3 bullish / 0 bearish tags), the chart repaired five months of damage in two days, and every bear argument was already inside the room when McKesson signed.

Skipped: independent confirmation of deal terms from filings (no tool access to the definitive agreement) — the $32.05 figure rests on social-media coverage citing Reuters/WSJ. Residual risk the user must know: if the deal breaks, downside is ~-24% to the pre-gap base; upside is hard-capped at $32.05.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case — OPCH (Option Care Health, Inc.)

I'll give the bull credit for honesty: their own framing concedes my core point before I even make it. They describe OPCH as "a merger-arb-style instrument with a hard cash ceiling at $32.05" and ~3.4% gross remaining upside against ~-24% downside on a deal break. That asymmetry — roughly 7:1 downside-to-upside — is the entire bear case in their own words. The only thing standing between that trade and disaster is the assumption that a signed deal equals a closed deal. History says otherwise.

## The asymmetry is the argument

At $31.01 you are paying 96.8% of the takeout price. You are not buying a business — you're underwriting deal-completion risk for a ~$1.04 spread. Every dollar of fundamental upside is already gone; the market captured it on 10-06. The bull asks me to prove the deal fails. I don't have to. I only have to show the *probability-weighted* math is unfavorable: if the deal closes, you earn ~3.4%; if it breaks, you lose ~24%. The break-even implied probability is ~88%. Anything below that — even a healthy 10% break risk — makes this a negative-expectation trade. And bear in mind: the "no evidence of break risk" claim cuts both ways — two of three sentiment sources and ALL news feeds returned no data for this window. The bull is arguing absence of evidence is evidence of absence on a dataset that was mostly dark.

## Deal-break risks are real, not hypothetical

- **Financing risk exists by construction.** This is a McKesson + CD&R take-private — PE co-sponsors mean leverage. The world-affairs report couldn't even pull a 10-year yield or fed funds rate (FRED unavailable). Nobody in this debate has verified the rate environment the debt financing was priced against. If credit conditions moved between signing and close, that's the classic break vector — and it's completely unexamined.
- **Regulatory/antitrust exposure is unanalyzed.** McKesson is a strategic buyer in the drug channel buying the largest US home-infusion provider. Channel consolidation deals draw FTC scrutiny — this administration's posture toward healthcare M&A is unverified in our data precisely because no news source returned anything. The bull's "no regulatory evidence exists" is a data gap dressed up as diligence.
- **The ~3.4% spread itself is a signal.** The market is not stupid. A definitive cash deal trading a full point under the takeout price is the market pricing residual risk — arb desks are demanding compensation for exactly the scenarios the bull waves away. If the deal were a lock, the spread would be tighter.
- **No confirmation of terms.** Per the sentiment report, the $32.05 figure comes from StockTwits posts citing Reuters/WSJ — 26 messages, 3 labeled. The fundamentals report explicitly could not confirm valuation multiples or insider activity. Nobody has read the merger agreement: termination fees, MAC clauses, financing contingencies, go-shop provisions — all unknown.

## The pre-deal fundamentals are worse than the bull admits

Strip the deal away and look at what the standalone company had become — because that's what you own if the deal breaks:

- **Revenue declined YoY in consecutive quarters** — Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 both ~$1,351M, a −4.6% YoY print in Q1 2026. First decline in the combined company's history. The growth narrative was already dead before the buyout.
- **Negative operating leverage is compounding:** operating income down to $73M from $85M, net income $45M vs $52M, EPS $0.29 vs $0.31. Margins compressing ~60–100bps with flat revenue — the trajectory, not the level, is the problem.
- **Cash balance nearly halved:** $413M → $177M in three quarters, against ~$2B in liabilities. Q1 operating cash flow was *negative* (−$12M). The bull calls the drawdown "deliberate" — spending cash on buybacks while revenue shrinks is a choice that looks clever only if the business stabilizes.
- **The April crash is unexplained.** The stock lost 24% in a day on 2026-04-30 and nobody in this dataset has identified why. Whatever that event was — likely an earnings/guide disaster consistent with the revenue stall — it lives in the stock's recent history. A deal break doesn't return OPCH to a healthy ~$23 base; it returns it to a deteriorating one.

## Refuting the bull point-by-point

- **"Sophisticated buyers validated the price."** Buyers validate the price *to them*, including synergies a standalone can't capture — the bull said this themselves. McKesson can pay $32.05 because it pockets channel synergies; that says nothing about what OPCH is worth alone. And PE sponsors walk away from deals when the math moves — that's what termination-fee clauses exist for.
- **"The growth stall is already inside the deal price."** Exactly — which means it's inside the ~$23.40 break level too, and arguably should push it lower on a re-rating of a now-proven declining business. The downside reference the bull uses assumes the market prices a break at the old base; a broken deal on declining fundamentals often gaps *through* the base.
- **"The stock held $31 — acceptance."** Acceptance of a deal price, yes. That's circular: the stock holds near $31 precisely because the deal caps it there. It tells you nothing about downside support, which sits at $29.80 (thin), then $26.43, then air to $23.40. RSI 83.7 and price 29% above the 50 SMA mean *no technical structure exists* between here and the pre-gap zone — on a break, there is no bid.
- **"Sentiment is uniformly positive."** 3 bullish tags in a 26-message sample, with Yahoo and Reddit both returning nothing. That's not uniform sentiment — that's one thin dataset. And the only substantive posts are arb-spread commentary, i.e., professionals pricing the very break risk the bull dismisses.

## Bottom line

The bull and I agree on the facts: capped upside of ~3.4%, downside of ~-24%, deteriorating fundamentals underneath, unverified deal terms, and a data environment with more holes than evidence. Where we differ: they call a signed agreement a conclusion; I call it a contingent claim priced near full value. The bear case on OPCH isn't that the deal breaks — it's that at $31.01 you are paid almost nothing to bear a break risk nobody here has actually measured, in a stock whose standalone business has already stopped growing. Chasing this at market is buying someone else's exit at the cap.

Skipped: no verification of the merger agreement's actual terms, financing structure, or regulatory posture — none of our data sources could confirm them, and neither could the bull's. Residual honesty: if the deal closes cleanly on a normal timeline, the bear thesis caps out at being right-but-unprofitable — the upside forgone is only ~3.4%.
